transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-12-02 14:30 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya, Connor, Elena (Redwood); Samir, Lena, David (Argosy)

Summary (auto): quick recap of outage, RCA review, mitigation plan, action items.

00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. we wanted to run through the postmortem, confirm the mitigations and line up the benchmarks.
00:16 Samir (VP Eng): thanks Maya. yeah, rough week. We had a pretty big customer-impacting degradation on Tuesday, so looking to make sure we don't see repeats.
00:27 Connor (SE): super sorry again for the blast there — we've been digging into the traces and the runtime logs. early summary: root cause was the idle-connection bug in our inference runtime combined with a traffic spike and a misconfigured retry policy on your side. the combination led to a burst of 502/503s and connection churn.
00:46 Lena (SRE): can you unpack the "idle-connection" thing? we've seen timeouts but the app didn't show backend load.
00:53 Connor (SE): yeah, so quick tl;dr — when a model variant had been idle for >10m, the server-side connection pool would drop kernels and then on warmup we'd occasionally hit an error path during kernel re-init which caused requests to fail fast instead of queuing and retrying. on top of that, your fleet retry policy had a low retry budget and the client retried too aggressively from the fronted LB, which amplified the errors into a larger outage.
01:20 David (Security): that error path — is it a crash or an auth error? anything that could have leaked data or logs?
01:29 Connor (SE): no PII exposure. the failure was internal to the runtime re-init; logs show stacktraces around kernel cache hits/misses. we capture call traces but we redact payloads by default — we verified no request bodies were persisted in the error logs.
01:45 Samir: ok good to know on the data side. why didn't our monitoring catch the kernel re-init spikes earlier?
01:53 Elena (CSM): part of this is that the re-init latency looked like normal cold-starts in the dashboard and we didn't have alerting for the specific error-class. so we need a metric and an alert.
02:05 Maya: right — action item for us: add a heartbeat/error-class metric so you can page before it cascades. Connor, can you outline the near-term mitigations?
02:14 Connor: yeah. short-term: disable the aggressive client-side retry for the affected route (we recommended reducing parallelism and adding exponential backoff), deploy a hotfix to ensure the runtime queues on kernel re-init instead of failing, and add per-route circuit breakers so a single model variant's failures don't cascade region-wide. medium-term: increase KV cache residency for your high-traffic prefixes, and add warmup probes for pinned model variants. long-term: a runtime patch to avoid the kernel drop path and a config UI to control idle thresholds.
02:45 Lena: KV cache residency, can you explain the customer impact? we rely on prefix caching for the low-latency flows.
02:53 Connor: with prefix/KV cache mis-tuning, we saw a lot more kernel reloads because the runtime evicted relevant KV entries during the traffic churn. that raised warmup frequency, which then hit the re-init bug more often. by increasing residency for the top N prefixes (we'll identify them in the benchmark), the warmup rate drops and you keep latency stable.
03:12 David: on auditing — you mentioned logs redaction. would Redwood be able to provide a SOC2 artifact or more specifics?
03:20 Maya: yes, we have our SOC 2 Type II and ISO attachments — we'll share the artifacts as part of the postmortem package. we'll also include your requested audit log retention options and options for pushing logs to your SIEM via secure delivery.
03:36 Samir: good. what's the timeline for the hotfix?
03:40 Connor: we can push a staged hotfix to Dedicated pools by 2027-12-07 if we get the go-ahead; it'll contain the queue-on-reinit behavior and a guard for the kernel drop path. we also want to run a canary with Argosy traffic slice first.
03:53 Elena: what's the canary plan look like?
03:55 Connor: step 1, we take an anonymized traffic subset from Argosy (Samir to provide) and run it against a dedicated test pool with the hotfix. step 2, run 24 hours of traffic with stress signals and watch error budgets. step 3, promote to production with gradual rollout and circuit-breaker controls.
04:18 Samir: ok, we can provide the sample traffic, but we need to ensure PHI is removed — we'll filter.
04:24 David: and security will want the logs for the canary preserved and delivered to our SIEM. is that doable?
04:30 Maya: yes — we can set up secure delivery of canary logs and grant Argosy read-only access during the test.
04:36 Samir: curious on the Dedicated vs Hosted question — is this bug more likely to hit Dedicated customers?
04:42 Connor: it can hit both. the key vector is kernel churn and idle thresholds. Dedicated gives you more configurability (longer idle thresholds, pinned processes) which reduces the surface area. Hosted customers see the same runtime but with shared pools and our autoscaling policies; we will apply the hotfix across both but Dedicated customers can opt into stronger residency guarantees.
05:05 Elena: can you also walk us through rate-limiting/circuit-breaker defaults? we want to make sure one route can't starve others.
05:13 Connor: default circuit breakers are conservative; we'll recommend per-route concurrent requests limits and a half-open probe strategy. we'll provide suggested values based on your traffic profiles after the benchmark.
05:28 Samir: ok let's talk about SLA credits — we hit a lot of customer-impact minutes. how will Redwood handle that?
05:35 Maya: we want to make it right. I'm going to loop legal and ops after this call to propose a remediation/credit for that incident window per our SLA terms. we'll send a formal credit proposal and include the postmortem artifacts.
05:49 Lena: thanks. a few nitty bits — we also saw elevated tails on token latency even outside the outage window, any root cause there?
05:58 Connor: likely related — warmup frequency plus suboptimal kernel selection for some long-sequence requests. part of the medium-term plan is smarter kernel selection based on sequence distribution and a short-lived compilation cache to reduce tail latencies.
06:15 David: on compliance — we'll want KMS integration for any private deployment keys. is Redwood supporting HSM/KMS options?
06:24 Maya: yes, we support KMS integrations and can enable customer-managed keys for Private deployments. we'll attach the KMS/HSM integration guide in the postmortem package.
06:34 Samir: cool. next steps recap?
06:36 Elena (CSM): Connor will kick off benchmark and hotfix canary. Elena to share postmortem doc and artifacts. Maya to coordinate SLA credit proposal. Samir to provide filtered traffic and error traces.
06:52 Connor: timeline again — hotfix canary by 2027-12-05 internal, staged push to dedicated canary 2027-12-06, target rollback/final rollout 2027-12-07 depending on canary health.
07:05 Samir: that's fine. please send the runbook for the canary and we'll book the maintenance window.
07:11 Maya: will do. anything else from Argosy?
07:14 Samir: no, thanks — appreciate the quick follow-up.
07:17 David: thanks all.
07:19 Maya: great, we'll share the doc and loop in legal/ops. meeting adjourned.
